description_full: Lockheed Martin Corporation, an aerospace and defense company, engages in the research, design, development, manufacture, integration, and sustainment of technology systems, products, and services in the United States, Europe, Asia, the Middle East, and internationally. The company operates through four segments: Aeronautics; Missiles and Fire Control (MFC); Rotary and Mission Systems (RMS); and Space. The Aeronautics segment offers combat and air mobility aircraft, unmanned air vehicles, and related technologies. The MFC segment provides air and missile defense systems; tactical missiles and precision strike weapon systems; logistics; fire control systems; mission operations support, readiness, engineering support, and integration services; and ground vehicles. The RMS segment offers military and commercial helicopters, surface ships, sea- and land-based missile defense systems, radar and laser systems, sea- and air-based mission and combat systems, command and control mission solutions, cyber solutions, simulation and training solutions, and services and support for surface ships. The Space segment provides satellites; space transportation systems; strategic, advanced strike, and defensive systems; and classified systems and services in support of national security systems. This segment also provides network-enabled situational awareness; and integrates space and ground global systems to help its customers gather, analyze, and securely distribute critical intelligence data. It primarily serves the U.S. government and international customers, as well as foreign military sales contracted through the U.S. government. The company was formerly known as The Lockheed Corporation and changed its name to Lockheed Martin Corporation in March 1995. Lockheed Martin Corporation was founded in 1912 and is based in Bethesda, Maryland.

financial_summary: Lockheed Martin Corporation is a large-cap industrials business with a $131.0B market cap on $75.0B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +4% over the past three years and +5% annually across the full decade, which puts it in mature, slow-growth territory.

Returns on capital run at 32% against a 7% cost of capital — a 25-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat, and 11% gross margins are typical of commodity economics where competitors can replicate the product cheaply.

The business throws off $6.9B in free cash flow — roughly 9 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.71× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 1.9× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage runs at 6.9×.

Shareholder yield of 4.7% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome.

sect: Its 10% operating margin is roughly in line with the Industrials median (9%).
It earns less of the sector's profit than its revenue share would suggest (0.94x).

The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.01 across 544 companies in the universe; the top four hold 9% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares have drifted higher, up 12% over the past year excluding the latest month.
The price sits mid-way through its 52-week range, 18% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 31% and a beta of 0.47, it is more defensive than the market.
Liquidity is deep, with about $607.0M traded a day.
In past sell-offs it fell 37% in the 2020 crash, 17% in the 2022 bear market and 51% in 2008.
val: The stock trades only 3% below its DCF fair value of $585, a thin margin of safety.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 31%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $447 to $802 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
Against its own history it is dear: the EBIT multiple sits 85% above its 10-year median.
Earnings yields are mixed: an FCF yield of 5.3% (above the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 5.2% (vs the 8% bar).
The 22 covering analysts target $661 on average, 17% above the price.
The price implies 2.0% annual cash-flow growth, 4pp less than the model expects.
prof: ROIC of 32% clears the cost of capital of 7.0% by 25pp, the mark of a value creator; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 0.32).
It runs a 11% gross margin and converts 9% of revenue into free cash flow.
Earnings quality looks solid: cash conversion of 1.71x.
ROE of 75% is amplified by 8.9x balance-sheet leverage (DuPont), so ROIC is the cleaner read on the business.
It spends 2.7% of revenue on R&D and 0.4% on stock compensation.
hlth: Leverage is moderate at 1.9x net debt to EBITDA ($4.1B of cash against $21.7B of debt), above the 1.5x gate, with interest covered 6.9x.
No distress or manipulation flags (Altman Z 3.5, in the safe zone).
growth: Revenue has compounded at 4.4% over 3 years, 2.8% over 5 years and 5.0% over 10 years.
Net reinvestment is nil (capex and working capital no more than cover depreciation), so fundamental growth is near zero.
Free cash flow has compounded 1.5% a year over five years, short of the 5% durability bar.
Forward indicators: a book-to-bill of 1.23 (orders outpacing sales), a backlog worth 2.6x annual revenue and deferred revenue up 17%.
Capex roughly matches depreciation (1.0x, 2.2% of sales), a maintenance pace.
Its Rule of 40 score is 12, below the 40 that marks a healthy growth business.
own: Insiders hold little stock (0.1%), and institutions hold 77%.
Insiders have only sold over the past year (20 sales, net $118K sold).
It returns 4.7% a year to shareholders (2.3% in buybacks and 2.5% in dividends).
The share count has shrunk 3.9% a year over five years, steadily raising each holder's stake.
It has paid a dividend for 42 consecutive years, raising it 2.5% a year over the last five.
people: With about 123,000 employees, each generates about $610K of revenue, 1.7x the Industrials median, and productivity has risen 3.2% a year.
That works out to $56K of free cash flow per employee.
CEO pay is $9.8M (16x revenue per employee).
